text:
kevin: Heads-up — the header-based version negotiation rollout (Accept-Version) caused a small spike in 5xxs during the NYC->us-east failover this morning. Thinking we should rollback the header path and switch to explicit ?api_version param for a simpler fallback. Thoughts?

shilpa: saw the spike. Telemetry shows mismatch with some old SDKs that strip unknown headers. They fell back to default v1 routing which then overloaded the v1 pool.

maria: can we do a targeted rollback? i.e. disable Accept-Version routing only for the cloud-edge loadbalancer and keep it elsewhere while we patch SDKs?

dan: rolling header negotiation back is trivial in router config, but we need a plan to avoid a config flip-flop causing more churn. suggest canary off -> monitor error budget -> full rollback.

rachel: dashboard note — created a short panel on console showing Accept-Version usage by client_id and by region (quick link: https://console.internal/redwood/dashboards/accept-version). we can watch client_id heatmap during canary.

kevin: good. propose this rollout plan: 1) flip Accept-Version routing off for 10% of traffic (route set) 2) wait 15m, check 5xx & p95 latency + quota throttle spikes 3) if healthy, expand to 50% 4) full disable. fallback rule: if router sees unknown/stripped header, use explicit param if present, else route to v2-compatible pool with short-circuit.

shilpa: minor update — some customers use a CDN that strips query params but preserves headers. switching to ?api_version could break them. we need to detect both and keep one canonical source of truth. maybe prefer explicit param > header > client metadata?

maria: can we avoid breaking CDNs by implementing a small header shim at the edge LB that reads ?api_version and re-sets X-Client-Version header before the router? that keeps internal logic header-first but survives stripped headers.

dan: edge shim is doable but adds a hot path. performance impact should be measured. small Go lambda between LB and router could copy param->header. here's a minimal snippet for the shim:```go
func copyVersion(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request){
  v := r.URL.Query().Get("api_version")
  if v!="" {
    r.Header.Set("X-Client-Api-Version", v)
  }
  proxy.ServeHTTP(w,r)
}
```

rachel: telemetry recommendation: emit a tag 'version_source' with values [param, header, inferred] and a boolean 'shim_applied'. that will let us see how many requests needed the shim and how many clients rely on each mechanism.

kevin: agree. add also a migration metric: client_version_staleness that counts clients reporting v1 vs v2 in the last 7 days. we can use that to gate full removal of v1 routes.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: rollback-accept-version-rollout v1 -> v2-shim-preview. CI: green. ETA: 8m.

maria: can we add a console UX nudge? when somebody with high usage has still v1, display a small banner with migration steps and a one-click opt-in to the shim. low friction for PLG customers.

shilpa: yes — but ensure we respect account-level override. also include quota implications in the banner (e.g., v2 may hit different token accounting).

dan: operational checklist for the rollback now: 1) create canary route at 10% 2) enable shim on edge for canary 3) enable telemetry tags 4) monitor dashboards for 30m 5) scale to 50% then 100% if stable 6) run post-mortem on SDKs that strip headers.

kevin: sounds good. i'll own rollout. shilpa will own telemetry, maria will own console nudge, dan will own edge shim. rachel can you add the dash panels to the runbook and set an alert on client_version_staleness delta > 10%/hr?

rachel: yep. alert set: severity P2 -> pager after 30m if deltas persist. added runbook steps and linked logs query.

kevin: thanks all. if we see more than 0.5% increase in 5xx during canary, we abort and revert. otherwise proceed on the timeline.

observability-bot: New alert subscription created: accept-version-rollout-watchers. Subscribed: kevin, shilpa, maria, dan, rachel.

maria: quick doc link for SDK teams — please add header preservation note to SDK migration guide: https://docs.internal/redwood/sdk-migration#headers-and-query-params

kevin: rolling canary now (10%). monitoring closely. :eyes:

shilpa: early signal: small drop in v1 pool QPS, no spike in 5xx yet. will report in 10m.

kevin: update 12m — p95 down 15ms, 5xx flat. moving to 50% per plan.

maria: 50% -> healthy. starting console banner cohort rollout to top-50 heavy users.

kevin: full disable complete. rollout marked success. we'll keep shim in place for 14 days then re-evaluate. closing thread after post-mortem draft in 24h. :tada:
